nodes.label: Market Data Ingestion Service
nodes.rationale: Sole component that knows what an external provider looks like, so the provider API key lives in exactly one service and swapping providers is a contained change. Explicitly not responsible for aggregation, business rules, or cross-restart deduplication (consumers are idempotent instead).

nodes.label: Market Data Processor
nodes.rationale: Separate from the Bar Aggregator because it is stateless and its failure mode (idempotent retry) differs from a stateful accumulator's. Commits offsets after the DB write so at-least-once duplicates are absorbed by ON CONFLICT (event_id) DO NOTHING.

nodes.label: Bar Aggregator
nodes.rationale: Runs as its own service in its own consumer group — the first second consumer of tw.market.trades.v1, which is what makes ADR-0001's fan-out argument true rather than intended. Kept separate from the Processor because it is stateful and its failure mode (lost in-memory bar state) is different.

nodes.label: Strategy Engine
nodes.rationale: Core contract is a pure function evaluate(state, bar) -> (state, signals) with no I/O and no ability to see data later than the bar, so the same implementation can be driven by a backtest driver and a live driver. This is what makes a backtest a meaningful predictor of paper-trading behaviour.

nodes.label: Backtest Runner
nodes.rationale: Runs as a worker rather than inside the API request cycle; the bar stream is a forward-only iterator so lookahead is structurally impossible. Backtesting deliberately bypasses Kafka because it is a batch job over data that already exists.

nodes.label: Execution Simulator
nodes.rationale: A single shared library used by both the backtester and paper trading. Building it twice is exactly how the two silently diverge; backtest and paper trading disagreeing about a fill is a bug, not a nuance.

nodes.label: Anomaly Detection Service
nodes.rationale: Two tiers in implementation order: a transparent robust z-score baseline that every later model must beat, then an IsolationForest. The wording constraint (anomaly_score, 'unusual activity', never manipulation/fraud) is a hard requirement, not a style preference.

nodes.label: Alert Dispatcher
nodes.rationale: Applies deduplication and cooldown per (rule, symbol) so one volatile morning does not produce four hundred notifications.

nodes.label: FastAPI API Gateway
nodes.rationale: The only component the browser talks to and the only inbound door. Read-only with respect to market data: no client-facing endpoint writes ticks, bars or anomalies; that write path exists only inside the trust boundary.

nodes.label: React + TypeScript Frontend
nodes.rationale: API types are generated from the FastAPI OpenAPI schema so a backend contract change breaks the frontend build rather than production. No global state library until one is demonstrably needed.

nodes.label: SyntheticProvider
nodes.rationale: A seeded random walk plus deterministic replay, used for all local development, CI and load tests. No API key, no rate limit, no network — which is what keeps every other phase unblocked when a provider surprises.

nodes.label: Vertical Slice First
nodes.rationale: A thin end-to-end path (data in → database → API → chart) exists before Kafka, before ML, before auth. Infrastructure is added when a concrete requirement forces it, never speculatively.

nodes.label: Every Technology Earns Its Place
nodes.rationale: Kafka, PostgreSQL and Redis each have a written ADR justification. If a component's justification collapses, the component goes.

nodes.label: Ports Before Adapters
nodes.rationale: External systems sit behind narrow interfaces so tests run without them and swapping a provider is a contained change. Proven in Phase 2: swapping the in-memory bus for Kafka required no change to IngestionService or MarketDataProcessor.

nodes.label: The Database Is the System of Record
nodes.rationale: Kafka is a transport and replay buffer with finite retention, not durable truth. Redis is disposable. This is why topic auto-creation (infinite retention) is switched off and why the API and frontend read only PostgreSQL.

nodes.label: No Invented Numbers
nodes.rationale: Every latency, throughput or accuracy figure must be produced by a benchmark in this repository with its methodology and hardware recorded. Until measured, a number does not exist.

nodes.label: Deterministic Where It Matters
nodes.rationale: Strategy evaluation, backtesting and execution simulation are pure and reproducible: same inputs plus same seed produce identical results.

nodes.label: Three Timestamps (occurred_at / ingested_at / recorded_at)
nodes.rationale: Never conflated: occurred_at drives all business logic and bar boundaries, ingested_at drives lag metrics, recorded_at drives auditing. Everything UTC as timestamptz; local time exists only in the browser's rendering layer (failure F12).

nodes.label: Kafka Event Envelope
nodes.rationale: One envelope on every topic; payload differs, envelope never does. Transport metadata at the top level lets a consumer read a message it cannot interpret and route it usefully rather than failing to parse the whole thing.

nodes.label: Deterministic event_id
nodes.rationale: event_id is derived from the event's own data, so normalizing the same trade twice yields the same id and UNIQUE(event_id) absorbs duplicates that originate at the provider. An earlier draft specified UUIDv7, which cannot deduplicate anything because a fresh one is generated each time; UUIDv7 remains the rule for entity primary keys only.

nodes.label: Topic Naming and Partition Keying
nodes.rationale: Keying is a correctness decision, not a performance one: symbol keys guarantee per-symbol ordering the aggregator and every strategy depend on; deployment_id keys stop a deployment's position inverting. Nothing is guaranteed across symbols and nothing claims otherwise.

nodes.label: At-Least-Once Delivery Semantics
nodes.rationale: Exactly-once via Kafka transactions is not worth its complexity and would not remove the need for idempotent writes anyway. Offsets are committed after the side effect, never before. Auto-commit has no setting because it is not a choice — it converts at-least-once into at-most-once.

nodes.label: Dead-Letter by Classification, Not Retry Count
nodes.rationale: A permanent failure is quarantined on the first attempt because retrying only delays the same answer; a retryable failure is never quarantined because dead-lettering during an outage converts a recoverable incident into a manual replay. There is no redrive tool, deliberately.

nodes.label: Trust Zones
nodes.rationale: Nothing in the internal plane is reachable from the public internet; market data enters only through the ingestion service's outbound connection, and the FastAPI gateway is the only inbound door.

nodes.label: Ownership Enforced in the Data Access Layer
nodes.rationale: Every query for a user-owned resource takes an actor and filters by user_id, so a route that forgets cannot leak. This is the defence against IDOR, the most likely real vulnerability in a system like this.

nodes.label: Redis: Justified Uses Only
nodes.rationale: Every cached key has a TTL and a documented invalidation trigger; TW_CACHE_ENABLED=false must leave the application fully correct. If a cache cannot be shown to reduce measured p95 latency, it is removed. Redis is never the system of record, a job queue or a session store.

nodes.label: Testing Strategy (Layers and Rules)
nodes.rationale: Tests exist to let the system be changed confidently, not to produce a coverage badge. Boundaries are faked, internals are not; the database is never mocked; coverage has no hard gate because a threshold encourages tests that assert nothing.

nodes.label: The Golden Backtest
nodes.rationale: A fixed strategy over a fixed committed fixture dataset with an expected equity curve; any unintended change to execution semantics fails it.

nodes.label: F7 — Duplicate Delivery
nodes.rationale: UNIQUE(event_id) and upserts cover consumers whose write is a replacement. A consumer that accumulates is not covered and needs its own mechanism — the aggregator records its stream position in the same transaction as the bars.

nodes.label: F11 — Out-of-Order / Late Market Data
nodes.rationale: A bounded lateness window emits market.bar.corrected rather than mutating history. Known open limitation: a multi-hour single-symbol backlog advances that symbol's watermark by hours in seconds, sealing every bar behind the jump and discarding queued trades into late_dropped. Fixing it means sizing the window in stream time or routing a detected backlog through the backfill path — recovery-mode behaviour deferred to Phase 11.

nodes.label: F13 — Bar Aggregator Restart Loses Open Bars
nodes.rationale: The open bar is written on every flush with is_final=false and reloaded at startup; redelivered trades already folded in are skipped by the recorded stream position.

nodes.label: Component Dependency Graph and Critical Path
nodes.rationale: Hard ordering constraints: the Execution Simulator must exist before either the backtester or paper trading; auth must land before any multi-user feature stores user data; the baseline detector must precede the ML detector because it is the model's benchmark; observability must precede benchmarking.

nodes.label: Decisions Deliberately Not Made Yet (D1–D20)
nodes.rationale: Recording open decisions prevents both premature commitment and the illusion that they were overlooked. Each names the trigger that should force the decision. D1 (Alpaca) and D12 (Recharts) are closed.

nodes.label: Assumptions That Must Remain Configurable
nodes.rationale: These are the things most likely to be wrong, so none may be hard-coded. Slippage, commission and the fill model materially change every backtest result, so they are stored on each backtest_run and deployment — a result can never be compared against one produced under different assumptions without the difference being visible.

nodes.label: Architecture Consistency Self-Audit
nodes.rationale: An architecture that contradicts itself is worse than none, so the document audits itself: every component appears in the data flow, every topic has a producer and consumer, every entity maps to a table, and no performance claim appears anywhere.

nodes.label: Not a Market-Manipulation Detector
nodes.rationale: The anomaly component detects statistically unusual activity relative to a symbol's own recent behaviour. It has no labelled ground truth and no validation against confirmed manipulation cases, and must never be described as detecting fraud, spoofing or manipulation.
